name: One Arm Joe
description: One Arm Joe (One-Armed Pete) is a one-card variant of Indian Poker. Each player receives one card face-down, holds it to their forehead so everyone else can see it but they cannot, then bets. Highest card at showdown wins the pot. A game of pure deduction and bluff.

overview.description: One Arm Joe (One-Armed Pete) is a one-card variant of Indian Poker. Each player receives one card face-down, holds it to their forehead so everyone else can see it but they cannot, then bets. Highest card at showdown wins the pot. A game of pure deduction and bluff.

history.origins: Indian Pokerâ€”cards held to the forehead so others see your card but you do notâ€”originated in America. The name has nothing to do with India; it refers to cards resembling a headdress. One Arm Joe and One-Armed Pete are regional names for the one-card variant.
timeline: Early 20th century: Indian Poker appears in home and bar games.
Present: Popular as a novelty poker variant in Dealer's Choice games.
history.cultural: A staple of 'Dealer's Choice' home games and bar poker; the spectacle of cards on foreheads makes it memorable.
history.evolution: The one-card version is the simplest; two- or three-card variants exist but add littleâ€”you see everyone else's strength, so it is mainly guessing your own from their actions.

setup.players: Two to eight players. The one-card variant is the basic form: each player is dealt one card face down, picks it up without looking, and holds it against the forehead so all others can see its value. A round of betting follows; at showdown the highest card among those who did not fold wins the pot. The game is usually played with 2–8; skills involved are probability and reading other players' actions and bets.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ace high; no suit ranking for ties.
setup.dealing: Each player antes. Dealer deals one card face-down to each player. Players pick up their card without looking, hold it facing outward, and place it against their forehead so all others can see it.

rules.objective: Win the pot by holding the highest card among those who did not fold, or by making all others fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. After cards are on foreheads, a round of betting occurs (ante, then betting as agreedâ€”limit, pot-limit, or no-limit). 2. Players act in turn: fold, check, call, or raise. 3. Showdown: all remaining players reveal. Highest card wins. Ties split the pot. 4. Optional: play lowest wins, or high-low split.
keyRules: Each player sees all other players' cards but not their own.
Ace is high; no suit order for tie-breakingâ€”tied cards split.
Match-pot variant: players declare stay or drop (simultaneously or in turn); best card of those who stayed wins; others who stayed must match the pot.
With simultaneous declaration, two high-card holders can both drop seeing each other; savvy players may exploit this.

strategy.basic: If everyone folds to you, betâ€”you might have the best hand. If you see several high cards on others' foreheads and they are betting, consider folding.
strategy.intermediate: Use opponents' reactions: if someone with a visible King hesitates, they may be worried you have an Ace. Bluff by betting confidently when others show weakness.
strategy.advanced: In match-pot, simultaneous declaration creates a game theory puzzle: two players with high cards may both drop, letting a lower hand win. Predict and exploit.
tips: The 'head dress' effect: your card is visible to everyoneâ€”your only signal is your betting.
In match-pot, staying in is costly if you lose; only stay when you think your card is likely best or everyone else will drop.
